CRLA No.887 of 2023
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Hon’ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Ms. Divya Jain and Ms. Manisha Bhandari, learned 
counsel for the appellants and Ms. Manisha Rana Singh, 
learned D.A.G. for the State. 
2. Instant appeal is preferred against the judgment and 
order dated 28.11.2023/01.12.2023, passed in Session Trial 
No.89 of 2012, State vs. Gauransh Uniyal and others, by the 
court of learned 6th Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun. 
By it, the appellants have been convicted under Section 302 
read with Section 34 of IPC. 
3. Heard the learned counsel for the parties on the Short 
Term Bail Application (IA No.04 of 2026). 
4. The appellant Gaurav Uniyal seeks short-term bail on 
the ground that he is suffering from high myopia in both 
eyes; the condition of his eyes is deteriorating day by day. 
He is on the verge of becoming blind. He needs to undergo 
refractive surgery for his eyes at PGI Chandigarh.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant would submit that 
the appellant is suffering from myopia and has to undergo 
refractive surgery at PGI Chandigarh so as to restore his 
vision, which is deteriorating day by day.
6. Learned State Counsel, on instructions, would submit  that, in fact, the appellant is suffering from myopia and the 
visual prognosis is guarded in view of pathological myopia. 
It is admitted that the appellant has been consulted by 
doctors for his low vision.
7. Having considered, purely on humanitarian ground, 
the short term bail is granted to the appellant for a period of 
two weeks from the date of his release, subject to his 
executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable 
sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the 
concerned court.
8. It is further directed that on expiry of the duration of 
short term bail, the appellant shall surrender before the court 
concerned.
9. List this case on 28.07.2026. 
10. Short term bail application stands disposed of 
accordingly.
(Siddhartha Sah, J.) (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 17.06.2026

orders.text:
UKHC010203322023
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
IA No.6 of 2026 For Second Short Term Bail Application
In
Criminal Appeal No. 887 of 2023
Gauransh Uniyal and Others ...... Appellants
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand ..... Respondent
Present:
Ms. Manisha Bhandari, Advocate for the appellant.
Mr. Siddhartha Bisht, A.G.A. for the State of Uttarakhand.
Coram: Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Hon’ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
The instant appeal has been preferred against 
judgment and order dated 28.11.2023/01.12.2023, passed in 
Sessions Trial No.89 of 2012, State Vs. Gauransh Uniyal and 
Others, by the court of 6th Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun. 
By it, the appellants have been convicted under Section 302 read 
with Section 34 IPC, and sentenced accordingly. The appellant￾Gaurav Uniyal has filed Second Short Term Bail Application, IA 
No.6 of 2026, on the ground that the condition of his eyes is 
deteriorating.
2. Heard on Second Short Term Bail Application, IA 
No.6 of 2026
3. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that 
the appellant Gaurav Uniyal was granted short term bail on the 
ground that the condition of his eyes was deteriorating; he is 
suffering from high myopia in both eyes; he is at the verge of 
becoming blind. He was to undergo refractive surgery for his eyes 
at PGI, Chandigarh. The appellant visited PGI Chandigarh, where 
some further tests have been advised and the next date for  2
consultation is 06.08.2026. It is argued that for another four 
weeks, the appellant may be granted short term bail. 
4. Fact remains that on the condition of the eyes of 
the appellant Gaurav Uniyal, he was granted short term bail. 
Some prescriptions have been filed along with the short term bail 
application.
5. Having considered, without adverting to the merits 
of the case, purely on the humanitarian ground, this Court is of 
the view that the appellant-Gaurav Uniyal may be enlarged on 
short term bail for a period of four weeks from the date of his 
release.
6. Let the appellant-Gaurav Uniyal be released on 
short term bail for a period of four weeks from the date of his 
actual release, on his executing a personal bond and furnishing 
two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of 
the court concerned.
7. It is further directed that on expiry of the period of 
short term bail, the appellant-Gaurav Uniyal shall surrender 
before the court concerned and intimation to that effect shall also 
be given to this Court.
8. The short term bail application stands disposed of, 
accordingly. 
9. List this matter on 16.09.2026, for hearing on the 
bail application, IA No.1 of 2023.
(Siddhartha Sah, J.) (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 05.08.2026 
 Ravi Bisht
